scope: Proposition 6.3 (A bounded weight evaluator) of the manuscript “An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities” (preprints/An-FPRAS-for-Common-Integer-Polymatroid-Bases-with-Binary-Capacities-October-5-2026/polymatroid-fpras.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 114 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c14d087890444879), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 32. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Given a profile in the entire slice S, rational 0 < ρ, β < 1, and a rational power s ∈ [0, 1] with denominator qs, there is an evaluator using fresh random bits and returning a strictly positive rational ˆ︁ hs such that P [︁ (1 − ρ)hs ≤ ˆ︁ hs ≤ (1 + ρ)hs]︁ ≥ 1 − β. Its output length, number of rank queries, and other bit operations are bounded on every execution by fixed polynomials in N, the input encoding lengths, ρ−1, log(β−1), and qs. In particular an equally spaced schedule with a polynomial number of phases has polynomially bounded denominators. Moreover J admits a deterministic positive rational approximation ˆ︁ J with | log( ˆ︁ J/J)| ≤ N−7 in polynomial work.
